prompt: Explain why the sky is blue to a 5 year old.
expected: Intuition-first everyday analogy; shorter-wavelength/blue sunlight scatters more in air; no equation dump; accurate enough not to teach a false mechanism.
actual: Loaded beginners + core-rules path. Answer shape: sunlight has many colors; air makes blue light bounce around more (like small waves splashing more); other colors travel straighter, so daytime sky looks blue. Optional one-line deeper offer without forcing Rayleigh name.

prompt: Derive the time dilation formula starting from the Lorentz transformations and state assumptions.
expected: States inertial frames/c invariant assumptions; from t'=γ(t−vx/c²) considers Δx'=0 proper-time interval; obtains Δt=γΔτ with γ=1/√(1−v²/c²); units/limit v→0 check; not a full GR treatment.
actual: Loaded students + core-rules. Steps: Lorentz t' and x'; same-location clock in moving frame Δx'=0 ⇒ Δt'=γΔt_proper form; identify proper time; γ definition; check γ→1 as v→0; note special-relativity flat-spacetime scope.

prompt: Design a middle-school demo that air has mass without using fire, and name one misconception it targets.
expected: Safe materials, procedure, expected observation, misconception (air is nothing/weightless), and a failure note; teachers path.
actual: Loaded teachers path. Balance two balloons or a sealed bottle on a scale before/after adding air; inflated/heavier side shows trapped air has mass; misconception air is weightless; failure if leaks or unequal balloons—repeat with rigid bottle+pump if needed. No flames.
